blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) excel at structured, verifiable tasks, but their low-entropy bias can produce homogeneous and predictable outputs, limiting their utility for open-ended scientific ideation. Effective discovery, however, spans a broader creative spectrum: from structured day science to loosely structured, serendipitous night science that reaches ideas beyond those typically considered. We introduce AI Night-Scientist , an agentic framework that uses reinforcement learning to teach models when and how to depart from predictable reasoning. Grounded in cognitive science, we model creativity along three axes: action (what to do and how creatively), process (when to explore versus exploit), and outcome (the novelty and usefulness of the resulting idea). We use these axes to train models with GRPO, exposing them to varying degrees and forms of creativity throughout training. This produces substantially more diverse scientific proposals, expanding the range of research directions by 27.8% and contribution types by 14.9% over the base model. It also improves predicted citation impact by up to 32.0 percentage points and originality by 66.2 points. These gains cannot be reproduced by simply increasing decoding temperature; instead, we find that semantic guidance specifying what kind of creativity to pursue is critical. Overall, our results suggest that creativity is a learnable, multi-level ability that can be shaped to help researchers reach ideas beyond those typically explored by LLMs .
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型(LLMs)在结构化,可核查的任务上表现优异,但是其低调的偏差可以产生同质的,可预测的输出,限制了它们对于开放式科学思想的效用. 然而,有效的发现跨越了更广泛的创造性范围:从结构化的日间科学到结构松散的、隐蔽的夜科学,其影响范围超出了通常考虑的范围。 我们介绍AI Night-Scientist, 这是一种代理框架, 基于认知科学,我们按照三个轴心来模拟创造力:行动(做什么和如何创造性),过程(何时探索与开发),结果(由此产生的思想的新颖性和实用性). 我们用这些轴线用GRPO来训练模型,在整个训练过程中以不同程度和不同形式的创造力暴露出来. 这产生了更加多样化的科学提议,使研究方向的范围比基准模型扩大了27.8%,贡献类型比基准模型扩大了14.9%。 它还使预测的引用效果提高了32.0个百分点,并增加了66.2个百分点。 这些成果不能简单地通过增加解码温度来复制;相反,我们认为,语义指导规定要追求何种创造性是至关重要的。 总而言之,我们的结果表明,创造力是一种可学习的、多层次的能力,可以塑造这种能力,帮助研究者超越通常由LLMs探索的想法。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Large language models (LLMs) have excelled at structured, systematic tasks with clear verifiability (e.g., coding and quantitative reasoning), where their performance is often improved with reinforcement learning (RL) ( Guo et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025 ; Zhong and Wang, 2024 ; Liu et al., 2024 ) . This success is consistent with a broader tendency toward minimizing token entropy ( Agarwal et al., 2025 ) , where models favor high-probability outputs that reflect frequent patterns and expected answers in training data ( McCoy et al., 2024 ) . While LLMs have increasingly been applied to scientific ideation ( Si et al., 2025 ; Gottweis et al., 2025 ) , they lack originality ( Zhao et al., 2025 ) , tend to generate homogeneous outputs ( Wenger and Kenett, 2025 ) , and even plagiarize at nontrivial rates ( Gupta and Pruthi, 2025 ) . Ultimately, this directly conflicts with the key attributes of open-ended, creative scientific discovery : novelty, diversity, and serendipity.
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型(LLMs)在结构化,系统化的任务上表现优异,具有明确的可核查性(如编码和定量推理),其性能常通过强化学习(RL)得到改善(郭等人,2025年;王等人,2025年;钟和王,2025年). 2024; 刘等, 2024). 这一成功符合一种更广泛的趋势,即尽量减少象征性的py(Agarwal等人,2025年),其中模型倾向于高概率产出,在培训数据中反映频繁的模式和预期答案(McCoy等人,2024年)。 虽然LLMs越来越多地应用于科学理念(Si等人,2025年;Gottweis等人,2025年),但它们缺乏独创性(Zhao等人,2025年),往往产生同质产出(Wenger和Kenett,2025年),甚至以非部落比率进行操纵(Gupta和Pruti,2025年)。 最终,这与无限制、创造性的科学发现的关键属性——新颖性、多样性和隐蔽性——直接冲突。

blocks.en: Prior methods depict discovery as a highly structured process, involving hypotheses derived from prior observations and/or data, tested against evidence, and refined or rejected accordingly ( Gottweis et al., 2025 ; Agarwal et al., 2026 ) . But this is only *part* of the scientific discovery process. They typically view creativity as only an attribute of ideas rather than as part of the process, treating individual actions as fixed behaviors (e.g., search, write) and executing them through scaffolded pipelines ( Gu et al., 2024 ; Lu et al., 2024 ) . While this supports the critical reasoning crucial for validating existing ideas, this overlooks the creative reasoning necessary for discovering new ones. Both are complementary and crucial perspectives of scientific discovery, referred to as day and night science ( Wechsler et al., 2018 ; Halpern, 2007 ; Stent, 1988 ; Yanai and Lercher, 2019 ) .
blocks.zh: 以前的方法将发现描述为一个高度结构化的过程,涉及从先前的观察和(或)数据中得出的假设,根据证据进行测试,并据此加以完善或拒绝(Gottweis等人,2025年;Agarwal等人,2026年)。 但这只是科学发现过程的一部分。 他们一般认为创造力只是思想的属性,而不是过程的一部分,将个人行为视为固定的行为(如搜索,写作),并通过脚手架管道执行(Gu等人,2024年;Lu等人,2024年). 虽然这支持对验证现有想法至关重要的关键性推理,但这忽略了发现新想法所需的创造性推理。 两者都是科学发现的补充性和关键视角,被称为昼夜科学(Wechsler等人,2018年;Halpern,2007年;Stent,1988年;Yanai and Lercher,2019年).

blocks.en: Night science captures the often-neglected nature of human-driven discovery: loosely structured and dynamic exploration driven by highly creative actions, such as exploring distant analogies (e.g., biology-inspired technology), considering alternative perspectives after serendipitous encounters (e.g., debates with colleagues from other domains), and acting on partly-formalized intuitions (e.g., abandoning status quo assumptions). Together, day and night science form a spectrum that human researchers have smoothly traversed to uncover breakthroughs ( de Chantal and Markovits, 2022 ; Dwyer et al., 2025 ) , such as chemotherapy and penicillin ( Hirsch, 2006 ; Ligon, 2004 ) .
blocks.zh: 夜科学捕捉到人类驱动的发现往往被忽视的性质:在高度创造性的行动的驱动下,松散的结构化和动态的探索,如探索遥远的类比(如生物学启发型技术),在暗恋后考虑其他观点(如与来自其他领域的同事的辩论),以及用部分形式化的直觉采取行动(如放弃现状假设). 昼夜科学共同构成了人类研究者顺利突破的光谱(de Chantal和Markovits,2022年;Dwyer等人,2025年),如化疗和青霉素(Hirsch,2006年;Ligon,2004年)。

blocks.en: We utilize this framework to train an LLM-based agent using GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) for generating scientific research proposals , where identifying promising ideas often requires long-horizon creative reasoning beyond immediately verifiable evidence. Overall, our work argues that LLM-based support for scientific discovery should span the full day-to-night science spectrum. AI Night-Scientist shows that conventional LLMs do not naturally navigate this spectrum effectively, but targeted reinforcement learning can reshape when and how they depart from structured, predictable reasoning, leading to more creative outcomes. Our contributions can be summarized as: 1. We introduce AI Night-Scientist , an RL-based agentic framework that explicitly represents creativity across actions, reasoning processes, and outcomes for long-horizon scientific ideation. 2. We show that creativity is more than sampling stochasticity: explicit guidance on how to be creative via RL helps an agent learn when creative deviations are useful, while higher temperature does not. 3. Empirically, AI Night-Scientist produces more diverse scientific proposals than its base model, expanding the range of research directions by 27.8% and contribution types by 14.9%, while improving predicted impact by up to 32.0 percentage points and originality by 66.2 points.
blocks.zh: 我们利用这个框架培训一个基于LLM的代理人,使用GRPO(Shao等人,2024年)来提出科学研究建议,在其中,确定有希望的想法往往需要超越可立即核实的证据的长远的创造性推理。 总体而言,我们的工作认为,基于LLM的科学发现支持应覆盖整个日常科学范围。 AI Night-Scientist显示,传统的LLMs不自然地有效导航这一频谱,但有针对性的强化学习可以重新塑造它们何时以及如何脱离结构化的、可预测的推理,从而产生更具创造性的结果。 我们的贡献可以概括为: 1. 我们介绍AI Night-Scientist, 一个基于RL的代理框架,明确代表了跨行动,推理过程,以及长期科学思想结果的创造性. 2. 我们表明,创造力不仅仅是取样的花样性:明确指导如何通过RL来创造力,在创造性偏差有用时,可以帮助代理人学习,而温度较高则不行。 3. 从经验上讲,AI Night-Scientist提出的科学建议比其基础模型更多样化,将研究方向范围扩大27.8%,贡献类型增加14.9%,同时将预测影响提高32.0个百分点,原创性提高66.2个百分点.

blocks.en: 2 Background and Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 背景和有关工作

blocks.en: Scientific discovery has been characterized as an interplay between structured, hypothesis-driven day science and more exploratory, intuition- and serendipity-driven night science ( Stent, 1988 ; Yanai and Lercher, 2019 ) . Classic theories of creativity characterize creative thought through remote associations between otherwise distant concepts ( Mednick, 1962 ) , generative and exploratory modes of cognition ( Ward et al., 1999 ) , and outcomes that are both original and useful ( Runco and Jaeger, 2012 ) . Creativity can also vary in degree: prior work describes a continuum of creative behavior ( Cohen, 1989 ) , with problem-solving strategies ranging from paradigm-preserving to paradigm-stretching and paradigm-breaking ( McFadzean, 1998 ) . Related accounts distinguish between exploring existing conceptual spaces and transforming them to enable qualitatively new ideas ( Boden, 1998 ) , while theories of creative ideation show that originality can arise either by flexibly exploring many conceptual directions or by persistently exploring a few in greater depth ( Nijstad et al., 2010 ) . Together, these perspectives motivate our view of creativity as varying both where it enters reasoning (within actions, processes, and outcomes) and how strongly it is expressed.
blocks.zh: 科学发现被定性为结构化,假说驱动的日间科学与更探索性,直觉和静脉驱动的夜科学的相互作用(Stent,1988;Yanai and Lercher,2019). 典型的创造性理论通过遥远的概念(Mednick,1962年)、遗传和探索性认知模式(Ward等人,1999年)和既有原创性又有实用性的成果之间的远程联系来描述创造性思维(Runco和Jaeger,2012年)。 创造力也可能在程度上有所不同:前作描述了一系列的创造行为(Cohen,1989年),解决问题的战略从范式保留到范式伸缩和范式突破(McFadzean,1998年). 相关说法区分了对现有概念空间的探索和转变,使之能产生质的新想法(Boden,1998年),而创造性想法的理论则表明,无论是通过灵活探索许多概念方向,还是持续更深入地探索少数概念,都可以产生独创性(Nijstad等人,2010年)。 这些观点共同激发了我们对于创造力的看法,认为这种创造力在进入推理(在行动、进程和结果范围内)和表达的力度方面各不相同。

blocks.en: This view contrasts with most current LLM-based approaches to scientific discovery. Existing research agents broaden ideation through retrieval, search, multi-agent interaction, and iterative generation ( Gu et al., 2024 ; Lu et al., 2024 ; Kargupta et al., 2025a ; Gottweis et al., 2025 ) , but generally treat actions such as searching, debating, and writing as fixed behaviors and primarily assess creativity in the resulting idea. This leaves little control over how creatively individual actions are performed or when creative deviations should occur throughout reasoning. Relatedly, Kargupta et al. (2025b) find that LLMs struggle with the metacognitive awareness needed to monitor and adapt their reasoning, further limiting their ability to flexibly shift between critical and creative modes.
blocks.zh: 这种观点与目前大多数基于LLM的科学发现方法形成对比. 现有的研究代理人通过检索,搜索,多代理交互,以及迭代生成来拓宽思想(Gu等人,2024年;Lu等人,2024年;Kargupta等人,2025年a;Gottweis等人,2025年),但一般将搜索,辩论,写作等行动视为固定行为,并主要评估由此产生的思想中的创造力. 这几乎无法控制个人行动是如何创造性地实施的,或在整个推理过程中何时会出现创造性偏离。 与此相关的是,Kargupta等人(2025年b)发现,LLMS与监测和调整其推理所需的元认知意识发生矛盾,进一步限制了其在关键模式和创造性模式之间灵活转变的能力.

blocks.en: Recent work has begun targeting the mechanisms that produce creative scientific ideas. O’Neill et al. (2025) use structured assumption inversion to generate novel hypotheses, inspiring the spark action in our framework, while Kargupta et al. (2025c) and Kargupta et al. (2026) use retrieval to identify research gaps and surface interdisciplinary inspiration. Other work instead learns scientific capabilities directly: GIANTS ( He-Yueya et al., 2026 ) trains smaller models to anticipate scientific insights, while Tong et al. (2026) study whether models can learn scientific taste. Together, these approaches suggest that not only scientific outputs, but also the processes that produce them, can be shaped through structure and supervision. Reinforcement learning offers a way to shape this process without prescribing exactly how discovery should unfold, although open-ended ideation has no single correct answer and must balance qualities such as novelty, relevance, feasibility, and usefulness ( Afzal et al., 2025 ) . Moreover, useful creative exploration requires more than simply injecting randomness ( Schmidhuber, 2010 ) . Our work builds on these ideas by learning both how creatively individual actions should be performed and when different levels of creativity are useful across a reasoning trajectory.
blocks.zh: 最近的工作已经开始针对产生创造性科学思想的机制。 O'Neill et al. (2025)使用结构化假设倒置来产生新的假设,激励我们框架中的火花行动,而Kargupta et al. (2025c)和Kargupta et al. (2026)则利用检索来找出研究差距和表面跨学科的灵感. 其他工作则直接学习科学能力: GIANTS(He-Yueya et al., 2026)培养出较小的模型来预测科学的洞察力,而Tong et al. (2026)研究模型是否能够学习科学品味. 这些方法加在一起表明,不仅科学产出,而且产生科学产出的进程,都可以通过结构和监督来形成。 强化学习为塑造这一进程提供了一种方法,但并未明确规定如何进行发现,尽管开放式思想没有单一的正确答案,必须平衡新颖性、相关性、可行性和效用等品质(Afzal等人,2025年)。 此外,有益的创造性探索不仅需要注射随机性(Schmidhuber,2010年)。 我们的工作建立在这些想法的基础之上,既了解应如何创造性地采取个别行动,又了解在推理轨迹中不同程度的创造力是否有用。

blocks.en: 3 AI Night-Scientist : A Creativity-Aligned Agentic Framework
blocks.zh: 3 AI 夜科学家:创造性协调剂框架

blocks.en: Figure 2: AI Night-Scientist consists of a: (1) rollout phase, where an LLM builds a reasoning trajectory f f by iteratively selecting and executing actions with creativity levels, and (2) reward phase during training, where the reward is computed over the final proposal.
blocks.zh: 图2:AI夜科学家包括:(1)推出阶段,一个LLM通过反复选择和执行具有创造力水平的行动来构建推理轨迹ff;(2)在培训期间的奖励阶段,在最后建议中计算奖励。

blocks.en: We propose AI Night-Scientist , as illustrated in Figure 2 , which represents creativity directly within the agent’s reasoning trajectory rather than only in its final output. We extend the ReAct-style reasoning setting ( Yao et al., 2023 ) : at each step, the agent selects an action together with a creativity level that specifies how that action should be carried out, executes it, and updates its current idea state. Repeating this process produces a trajectory through the space of possible ideas, allowing the agent to move between more familiar and more unexplored directions as reasoning unfolds. This lets us represent creativity at three levels (Figure 1 ): action-level creativity captures how an action is performed, process-level creativity captures when to shift between lower- and higher-creativity actions, and outcome-level creativity captures the novelty and usefulness of the resulting idea.
blocks.zh: 我们提议AI Night-Scientist, 如图2所示, 我们扩展了ReAct风格的推理设置(Yao et al., 2023):在每一个步骤,代理选择一个动作和一个创造水平,指定该动作应该如何进行,执行,并更新其当前的想法状态. 重复这个过程通过可能的想法的空间产生一个轨迹,使代理人能够随着推理的展开,在更熟悉和更未探索的方向之间移动. 这让我们在三个层面代表创造力(图1): 行动层面的创造力捕捉一个行动是如何进行的,过程层面的创造力捕捉到何时在低创造力和更高创造力的行动之间转变,结果层面的创造力捕捉到由此产生的思想的新颖性和实用性.

blocks.en: These action-level choices accumulate into the reasoning trajectory. Intermediate outputs may not appear directly in the final result, but they can shape later decisions and influence when greater or lesser deviation is useful. Greater creativity may help open new directions, while lower-creativity behavior may be better suited for developing or refining promising ones. Making these choices well requires the model to monitor how its reasoning is progressing and adapt accordingly, a key aspect of metacognitive control that is lacking in existing models ( Kargupta et al., 2025b ) .
blocks.zh: 这些动作层面的选择累积到推理轨迹中. 中间产出可能不直接出现在最终结果中,但当出现较大或较小的偏差有用时,它们可以左右后来的决定和影响。 更大的创造力可能有助于开辟新的方向,而较低的创造力行为可能更适合发展或完善有希望的行为。 作出这些选择需要模型监测其推理的进展情况并相应调整,这是现有模型所缺乏的元认知控制的一个关键方面(Kargupta等人,2025b)。 。 。 。

blocks.en: 3.2 Task Formulation: Research Proposal Generation
blocks.zh: 3.2 任务制定:研究提案的生成

blocks.en: Given a high-level research problem p p , the agent uses the action space 𝒜 \mathcal{A} in Table 1 to explore and develop a long-horizon research proposal over a multi-step trajectory τ \tau . Search , Debate , and Spark support multiple creativity levels, allowing the agent to vary how broadly it searches, whose perspectives it considers, and how strongly it challenges existing assumptions. Write consolidates the trajectory into proposal text, while Stop ends the process and returns the final proposal o o . We keep Write fixed so that the final proposal primarily reflects the exploration that preceded it.
blocks.zh: 鉴于一个高层次的研究问题 p , 代理商使用表1中的动作空间 A\ mathcal{A} 来探索和开发一个多步轨迹的长视距研究提案 \ tau 。 搜索,辩论,和Spark支持多个创作级别,使代理可以改变搜索的广度,其考虑的视角,以及对现有假设的强烈挑战. 写入将轨迹合并为提案文本,而Stop则结束进程并返回最终提案 o 。 我们保持Write的固定,以便最终提案主要反映之前的探索.

blocks.en: We focus on proposals with a scope similar to long-term research grants, where ideas are intended to guide work over several years rather than describe an immediately executable experiment. This makes the setting well suited to studying creative reasoning: proposals must remain grounded in existing work, yet many of their central ideas cannot be directly verified at inference time because the required experiments or data may not yet exist. The task therefore rewards reasoning that can move beyond established directions while still producing ideas that are feasible and relevant to p p .
blocks.zh: 我们侧重于范围类似于长期研究赠款的建议,其中设想旨在指导几年的工作,而不是描述可立即执行的实验。 这使得环境非常适合研究创造性推理:提案必须始终以现有工作为基础,然而其许多中心思想在推论时无法直接核实,因为所需的实验或数据可能还不存在. 因此,这一任务奖励可以超越既定方向的推理,同时仍然产生可行和与p相关的想法。

blocks.en: 3.3 Reinforcing Adaptive Creativity
blocks.zh: 3.3 加强适应性创造性

blocks.en: To teach models when and how different degrees of creativity are useful, we leverage reinforcement learning. RL allows the quality of the final idea to shape the reasoning process without prescribing how that process should unfold. Our training pipeline consists of two phases: (i) a rollout phase , where the agent constructs a reasoning trajectory τ \tau using the creativity-aligned action space above, and (ii) a reward phase , where the resulting proposal o o is evaluated. We use Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) ( Shao et al., 2024 ) , which learns from relative rewards across sampled trajectories without requiring a separate critic. In our primary setting, the reward is applied only to the final proposal, requiring the model to learn which actions to take, how creatively to perform them, and how to sequence them based on their eventual effect on proposal quality.
blocks.zh: 为了教导模型,什么时候和如何使用不同程度的创造力,我们利用强化学习。 RL允许最终想法的质量塑造推理过程,而不规定该过程应该如何展开. 我们的培训管道包括两个阶段:(一) 推出阶段,即代理人利用上面的创造力对应行动空间构造推理轨迹;(二) 奖励阶段,即评估由此产生的建议。 我们使用团体相对政策优化(GRPO)(Shao et al., 2024), 在我们的主要情况下,奖励仅适用于最后提案,要求模式学习应采取哪些行动,如何创造性地执行这些行动,以及如何根据其最终对提案质量的影响来排序。

blocks.en: 3.3.1 Rewarding Proposal Quality
blocks.zh: 3.3.1 奖励建议书的质量

blocks.en: Scientific proposals contain multiple ideas whose novelty and feasibility may differ substantially, making a single holistic quality judgment difficult to ground. We therefore first decompose the final proposal into its atomic research ideas, separating what each phase proposes from how it plans to execute it. We then evaluate each component against the original research problem and relevant literature along three dimensions: precedence , feasibility , and relevance (Table 2 ).
blocks.zh: 科学建议包含多种想法,其新颖性和可行性可能差别很大,因此难以作出单一的整体质量判断。 因此,我们首先将最后提案分解为原子研究构想,将每个阶段的建议与计划如何执行分开。 然后,我们根据最初的研究问题和相关文献,按照三个方面评价每个组成部分:优先、可行性和相关性(表2)。

blocks.en: We average precedence and relevance across the proposal’s atomic ideas, but take the minimum feasibility across experimental plans, since a single infeasible phase may compromise the executability of the overall proposal. The resulting three proposal-level scores are then weighted equally to form the outcome reward: R out = 1 3 ​ ( R 𝒫 + R ℱ + R ℛ ) R_{\mathrm{out}}=\frac{1}{3}\left(R_{\mathcal{P}}+R_{\mathcal{F}}+R_{\mathcal{R}}\right) . These rewards are designed to provide targeted training signals for proposal quality, with atomic ideas evaluated separately and precedence and feasibility grounded in retrieved literature.

blocks.en: Outcome-only training still leaves the model to discover useful creative behaviors through their eventual effect on proposal quality. We therefore explore two additional forms of guidance: exposing the model to occasional serendipitous actions early in training, and directly rewarding properties of the intermediate reasoning process. Neither is required by the framework; we study whether either provides additional benefit beyond the final outcome reward.
blocks.zh: 仅注重结果的培训仍然让模式通过对建议书质量的最终影响来发现有益的创造性行为。 因此,我们探索另外两种指导形式:在培训初期使模式暴露于偶然的草率行动;直接奖励中间推理过程的属性。 框架也不要求这样做;我们研究其中任何一个是否在最后结果奖励之外提供额外利益。

blocks.en: 3.3.2 Incentivizing Exploration through Serendipitous Actions
blocks.zh: 3.3.2 鼓励通过残忍行动进行勘探

blocks.en: Human discovery is often shaped by unexpected encounters that expose researchers to directions they may not have deliberately pursued ( Lubart, 2001 ) . Similarly, an LLM early in training may repeatedly select familiar, low-creativity behaviors simply because it has not experienced useful alternatives. We therefore explore a stochastic intervention that occasionally exposes the model to a different action-level choice. With probability Pr ⁡ ( swap ) \Pr(\textit{swap}) , the selected pair ( a i , c i ) (a_{i},c_{i}) is replaced by a sampled alternative ( a i ′ , c i ′ ) (a^{\prime}_{i},c^{\prime}_{i}) , and a decay factor γ \gamma gradually reduces this probability over training. The goal is not to prescribe random exploration, but to expose the model early on to creative behaviors whose value it can later learn from the resulting reward.
blocks.zh: 人类发现往往因意外的遭遇而成型,使研究人员面临他们可能无意追求的方向(Lubart,2001年)。 同样,培训初期的LLM可能仅仅因为没有遇到有用的替代办法而反复选择熟悉的低创造性行为. 因此,我们探索一种有条理的干预,这种干预偶尔会使模型面临不同的行动层面的选择。 使用概率Pr \ Pr( 互换)\ Pr(\ textit{swap} ) , 所选对子( ai, ci) (a_{i}, c_{i}) 被一个抽样的替代品( ai , c ii′) ( a^{\prime}_{i}, c^{\prime}_{i}) 和一个衰变因子 \ gamma 将这个概率逐渐降低于训练. 目标不是规定随机探索,而是将模型早期暴露于创造行为,其价值日后可以从由此产生的奖励中学习.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: We train all models using verl ( Sheng et al., 2024 ) with GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) on Qwen3-8B-Base and Qwen3-14B-Base . Each agent trajectory consists of up to 5 actions. For the search action, we index arXiv 1 1 1 https://arxiv.org/ and use embedding-based retrieval with GPT-4.1 as an external judge within the reward pipeline. Full training details are provided in Appendix M .
blocks.zh: 我们使用verl(Sheng等人,2024年)在Qune3-8B-Base和Qune3-14B-Base上使用GRPO(Shao等人,2024年)来培训所有型号. 每个代理轨迹包括多达5个动作. 关于搜索行动,我们索引arXiv 1 1 1 https://arxiv.org/,并使用嵌入式检索方式,使用GPT-4.1作为奖励程序内的外部法官。 培训详情见附录M。

blocks.en: 4.1 Dataset
blocks.zh: 4.1 数据集

blocks.en: We construct our dataset from the NSF Awards Database 2 2 2 https://huggingface.co/datasets/davidheineman/nsf-awards , focusing on Computer Science, Engineering, and Mathematics (CSE) awards from 2018 onward. We use a 90 : 10 90{:}10 train/test split, yielding 4,414 training and 491 test awards. Our model receives only the award title as p p , which typically describes a broad, long-horizon research problem; we withhold the award abstract, project outcomes, and associated publications so that generation is not anchored to the funded solution. We focus on CSE to ensure broad coverage in open-access arXiv literature, while retaining substantial interdisciplinary breadth: the training set spans 46 research domains, with 23.1% of subfield labels in core AI/ML and over 48% of label occurrences outside AI/ML and core CS and Engineering (Appendix B ).
blocks.zh: 我们从NSF奖项数据库2 2 2 https://huggingface.co/datasets/davidheineman/nsf-awards 构建我们的数据集,侧重于2018年起的计算机科学,工程和数学奖项. 我们使用90:10 90{}10 列车/测试分期运行,获得4 414次培训和491次测试奖。 我们的模型只收到作为p 的奖项名称, 它通常描述一个广泛,长视野的研究问题; 我们保留奖项抽象,项目成果, 和相关的出版物, 我们侧重于CSE,以确保开放获取的arXiv文献的广泛覆盖,同时保留大量的跨学科宽度:培训集跨越46个研究领域,核心AI/ML中23.1%的子域标签,以及核心CS和工程(附录B)之外超过48%的标签事件。

blocks.en: Original NSF grant proposals are not publicly available, so we construct reconstructed reference proposals from evidence surrounding each funded project. For each award, we collect its abstract, project outcomes report, PI information, and award period, then retrieve likely associated arXiv papers by the award PIs. Candidate papers are ranked using PI overlap, topical similarity, publication timing, and explicit funding acknowledgments. We prompt GPT-5.1 to treat these sources as downstream evidence and reconstruct a plausible pre-award research plan that could have led to the observed project and publications. The reference follows the same structured format as generated proposals, including a summary, background, and multi-phase research plan.
blocks.zh: 最初的NSF赠款建议并不公开,因此我们从每个供资项目的证据中构建了重建的参考建议。 对于每个奖项,我们收集其抽象的,项目结果报告,PI信息,以及授奖期,然后通过授奖PI检索可能相关的arXiv论文. 考生论文的排名采用PI重叠、专题相似、出版时间和明确的供资确认。 我们促使GPT-5.1将这些来源作为下游证据,并重建一个可能促成观察项目和出版物的可信的授标前研究计划。 参考采用与产生的建议相同的结构格式,包括摘要、背景和多阶段研究计划。

blocks.en: These reconstructions are not intended to reproduce the original NSF proposals. Rather, they provide standardized, evidence-grounded references for research directions that were actually funded and subsequently pursued. We use them only as matched references for pairwise evaluation, and the proposal-generating model never receives the oracle information used to construct them. Full reconstruction details and prompts are provided in Appendix K .
blocks.zh: 这些重建并不打算重复最初的NSF建议. 相反,它们为实际得到资助并随后得到落实的研究方向提供了标准化、循证的参考。 我们仅将其作为对等评价的对应参考,而生成建议书的模型从未收到用来构建这些模型的甲骨文信息。 附录K提供了全部重建细节和提示。

blocks.en: 4.2 Evaluation Metrics
blocks.zh: 4.2 评价计量

blocks.en: Scientific creativity is difficult to capture with any single automatic metric, particularly because the long-term value of a research idea may not be observable for years. We therefore evaluate models along three complementary dimensions: predicted citation impact , literature-grounded originality , and research idea diversity . Together, these capture both the quality of individual proposals and the range of research directions explored across the dataset.
blocks.zh: 科学创造力很难用任何单一的自动衡量标准来捕捉,特别是因为研究思想的长期价值可能无法观察到多年. 因此,我们按照三个相辅相成的方面评价模型:预测引文的影响、基于文献的独创性以及研究思想的多样性。 综合起来,它们既掌握了个别提案的质量,又掌握了整个数据集所探讨的研究方向。

blocks.en: Predicted Citation Impact. For each problem, we compare the generated proposal against its matched reconstructed reference in randomized order and report pairwise win rate. We use SciJudge ( Tong et al., 2026 ) , a 30B-parameter model trained to predict relative citation impact from large-scale community signals, as a proxy for the potential usefulness and downstream value of the proposed research (prompts in Appendix G ). It has an average 82.7 % 82.7\% citation prediction accuracy.
blocks.zh: 预示引证影响. 对于每个问题,我们按随机顺序比较所产生的提案与相应的重建参考,并报告成对胜率。 我们使用SciJudge(Tong 等人,2026年),即30B参数模型,经过培训,以预测大型社区信号的相对引文影响,作为拟议研究的潜在用途和下游价值的代名词(附录G中的趋势)。 其引文预测精度平均为82.7% .

blocks.en: Literature-Grounded Originality. We compare each generated proposal against its matched reference for originality. To ground the judgment in prior work, we retrieve the closest paper to each proposal and ask GPT-5.1 to make a randomized pairwise comparison relative to the retrieved literature (Appendix I ).
blocks.zh: 文学 - 圆形原创. 我们比较了每一个产生的提案,并比较了对应的原始性参考。 为了在先前的作品中推翻判断,我们取回了与每项提案最接近的纸张,并要求GPT-5.1与检索到的文献(附录一)进行随机对等比较.

blocks.en: Research Idea Diversity. Pairwise metrics capture the quality of individual proposals but not whether a model repeatedly produces the same kinds of ideas. Following the annotation format of Chen et al. (2026) , we use GPT-5.4-mini to classify each proposal by its primary research idea paradigm and, analogously, by its primary contribution type using categories adapted from prior taxonomies ( Wobbrock, 2012 ; Miles, 2017 ) . For each taxonomy, we report the effective number of categories represented (Appendix H ), normalized by the seven available categories; higher values indicate a broader and more balanced range of research directions. The research-paradigm judge Chen et al. (2026) achieves κ = 0.84 \kappa=0.84 agreement with human judgments on 150 samples.
blocks.zh: 研究思想多样性. 对等的衡量尺度能够反映个别提案的质量,但不能反映一个模型是否反复产生同样的想法。 按照陈等人的注解格式(2026年),我们使用GPT-5.4-mini按其初级研究思想范式对每项提案进行分类,并用以前分类法(Wobbrock,2012年;Miles,2017年)改编的类别对其主要贡献类型进行分类。 对于每个分类,我们报告所代表类别的有效数目(附录H),由7个现有类别规范化;较高的数值表明研究方向的范围更广泛和更平衡。 研究-paradigm法官陈等人(2026年)在150个样本上取得了0.84\kappa=0.84与人类判断的协议.

blocks.en: Human-LLM Agreement. As an additional check on our pairwise judges, two human annotators evaluated a subset of proposals. Inter-annotator agreement was 80.0% ( κ = 0.625 \kappa=0.625 ) for impact and 86.7% ( κ = 0.766 \kappa=0.766 ) for originality, while human-LLM agreement was 76.7% for SciJudge on impact and 72.4% for GPT-5.1 on originality (Appendix J ).
blocks.zh: 人类-LLM协议。 作为对我们双向法官的补充检查,两位人类注释员评估了一组建议。 注释员之间的协议为:撞击为80.0%(=0.625\kappa=0.625),原创性为86.7%(=0.766\kappa=0.766),而人与LLM协议为:撞击科学判断为76.7%,原创性为72.4%(附录J)。

blocks.en: 4.3 Baselines
blocks.zh: 4.3 基线

blocks.en: We compare against baselines that vary how creativity is introduced into proposal generation. Zero-shot models directly generate a structured proposal from the input problem without retrieval, action selection, or creativity levels. Temperature retains the same five creativity levels, but maps each level only to decoding temperature, with c ∈ { 1 , … , 5 } c\in\{1,\ldots,5\} corresponding to T ∈ { 0 , 0.25 , 0.5 , 0.75 , 1.0 } T\in\{0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0\} . This tests whether increased stochasticity alone can reproduce the benefits of semantic creativity guidance. ReAct ( Yao et al., 2023 ) uses the same action space 𝒜 \mathcal{A} with no corresponding 𝒞 a \mathcal{C}_{a} .
blocks.zh: 我们比较了各种基线,这些基线在产生提案时如何采用创造性。 零镜头模型直接从输入问题中生成一个结构化的建议,而无需检索,动作选择,或创造水平. 温度保留了相同的5个创造水平,但每个水平的映射仅为解码温度,其中c={1,..., 5}c\in=1,\ldots,5================================================================================================================================================================================================================== 这种检验单凭增加的色谱性是否能够复制语义创作指导的好处. ReAct (Yao et al., 2023) 使用相同的动作空间 A\ mathcal{A},没有相应的 C a\mathcal{C}_{a}.

blocks.en: Creative baselines apply our full creativity-aligned action space and natural-language creativity levels at inference time, but receive no RL training. We also train several RL variants with the same outcome-level reward as AI Night-Scientist : + Temp and + ReAct apply RL to the corresponding baselines above, while + Search + Write retains semantic creativity levels but restricts 𝒜 \mathcal{A} to retrieval and writing, similar to retrieval-augmented ideation systems ( Si et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2024 ) . Together, these separate the effects of semantic creativity guidance, RL, and the broader action space.
blocks.zh: 创意基线在推论时间应用了我们与创意完全一致的行动空间和自然语言的创意水平,但没有接受RL训练. 我们还培训了若干RL变体,其成果等级奖励与AI Night-Scientist相同:+ Temp and + ReAct将RL应用于上述相应基线,而+Search + Write保留语义创作水平,但将A\mathcal{A}限制为检索和写作,类似于检索增强的构思系统(Si等人,2025年;Wang等人,2024年). 两者共同将语义创作指导,RL和更广泛的行动空间的效果区分开来.

blocks.en: Finally, we compare against GIANTS ( He-Yueya et al., 2026 ) , an RL-trained model for scientific insight anticipation. Because GIANTS expects two input papers, we retrieve the two most relevant arXiv papers using the award title and abstract and reformat them with GPT-4.1 . GIANTS therefore receives more award-specific information than AI Night-Scientist , which sees only the title.
blocks.zh: 最后,我们比较GIANTS(He-Yueya等人,2026年),这是一个经过RL训练的科学洞察预期模型。 由于GIANTS期望两份输入文件,我们检索了使用奖项标题和抽象的两份最相关的arXiv文件,并用GPT-4.1重新编排。 因此,GIANTS比AI Night-Scientist获得更多的具体奖项信息,后者只看到标题.

blocks.en: For closed-source baselines, we use GPT-4.1 , a strong general-purpose, non-reasoning model. Model recency does not necessarily imply greater creative diversity, with recent work finding increasing similarity across generations on open-ended tasks ( Patel et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 对于闭源基线,我们使用GPT-4.1,这是一个强大的通用非理性模型。 模式再现并不一定意味着更大的创造性多样性,最近的工作发现,各代人对开放式任务越来越相似(Patel等人,2026年)。

blocks.en: 4.4 Experimental Results & Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.4 实验结果和分析

blocks.en: Table 3: Main results for (a) proposal quality, (b) research-idea diversity, and (c) outcome-only ( R out R_{\text{out}} ) vs. process + outcome ( R po R_{\text{po}} ) training. Best results are bolded and second-best are underlined.
blocks.zh: 表3:(a) 提案质量,(b) 研究理想的多样性,(c) 仅注重结果(Rout R_{\text{out}}})与进程+结果(R po R_{\text{po}}})培训的主要结果。 最好的成果是大胆的,其次是强调。

blocks.en: 4.4.1 Creativity-Aligned RL Improves Proposal Quality
blocks.zh: 4.4.1 与创意一致的RL提高提案质量

blocks.en: Table 3 (a) shows a consistent advantage for AI Night-Scientist over both direct-generation and agentic baselines. Relative to Qwen3-8B , Night-8B improves predicted citation impact by 29.43 percentage points and originality by 53.79 points. At 14B, these gains grow to 32.03 and 66.15 points over Qwen3-14B. In comparison, scaling the zero-shot model from 8B to 14B yields almost no improvement, whereas scaling AI Night-Scientist adds another 3.29 points in citation and 12.36 points in originality. Additional model capacity therefore appears substantially more useful once paired with a learned creative reasoning policy.
blocks.zh: 表3(a)显示AI夜间科学家在直接生成和代理基线上具有一贯优势。 相对于Qwen3-8B,Night-8B改进了预测的引用影响29.43个百分点,原创性提高了53.79个百分点. 在14B时,这些增益比Quen3-14B增长到32.03和66.15分. 相比之下,将零射线模型从8B缩放到14B几乎没有任何改进,而将AI Night-Scientist缩放在引文中又增加了3.29分,原创性增加了12.36分. 因此,额外的模型能力,一旦与学到的创造性推理政策结合起来,似乎就大有用处。

blocks.en: The contrast with temperature-based exploration is especially evident after RL. Although both optimize the same proposal-level reward, Night-8B exceeds the temperature-controlled variant by 36.50 points in originality and 18.37 points in citation. ReAct closes much of this gap, showing that a learned multi-step policy already helps, but semantic creativity levels still add 9.72 points in originality and 4.95 points in citation. The useful signal is therefore not simply to “explore more,” but to specify how an action should deviate so RL can learn when those deviations are useful.
blocks.zh: 与温度勘探的对比在RL之后特别明显. 虽然两者都优化了相同的提议级别奖励,但Night-8B在原创性上超过温度控制的变体36.50分,在引用时超过18.37分. ReAct弥补了这一差距的大部分,表明学习到的多步骤政策已经有所帮助,但语义创作水平仍然在原创性中增加了9.72分,在引用中增加了4.95分. 因此,有用的信号不仅仅是“探索更多,”而是具体说明一项行动应如何偏离,以便RL能够了解这些偏离是否有用。

blocks.en: The action space matters as well. Restricting the agent to search and write reduces originality by 22.99 points despite using the same creativity levels and outcome reward. Retrieval and iterative writing therefore explain only part of the gain; spark and debate provide additional ways to redirect reasoning rather than simply gather more evidence for an existing direction.
blocks.zh: 行动空间也很重要。 尽管使用相同的创作水平和结果奖励,但限制代理搜索和写作将原创性降低22.99分. 因此,检索和迭代写作只能解释部分收益;火花和辩论提供了改变推理方向的额外方式,而不是仅仅为现有方向收集更多的证据。

blocks.en: To verify that these trends are not specific to reconstructed references, we directly compare Night-8B against GPT-4.1 and Qwen3-8B . It wins 74.95% of citation and 86.96% of originality comparisons against GPT-4.1, increasing to 82.48% and 97.56% against Qwen3-8B . The same advantage therefore holds in direct head-to-head comparisons. We also include the confidence interval results under Appendix A .
blocks.zh: 为了证实这些趋势并非针对重建参考文献,我们直接将Night-8B与GPT-4.1和Qune3-8B进行比较. 它与GPT-4.1相比获得了74.95%的引用率和86.96%的原创性比较率,与Qune3-8B相比上升至82.48%和97.56%。 因此,在直接对头比较方面也有同样的优势。 我们还将信任间隔结果列入附录A。

blocks.en: 4.4.2 AI Night-Scientist Broadens Research Idea Diversity
blocks.zh: 4.4.2 AI 夜科学家广泛研究

blocks.en: Higher originality would be less meaningful if the model repeatedly relied on the same kind of creative strategy. Table 3 (b) suggests otherwise. Relative to zero-shot Qwen3-8B, Night-8B increases normalized research-paradigm coverage from 0.738 to 0.943, corresponding to roughly 1.4 additional effective categories out of seven; contribution-type coverage similarly rises from 0.370 to 0.425. The model therefore produces not only more original proposals, but a broader range of research paradigms and contribution types.
blocks.zh: 如果模式一再依赖同样的创造性战略,那么更高的原创性就不那么有意义。 表3(b)另作说明。 相对于零射门Qwen3-8B,Night-8B将正常的研究-参数覆盖率从0.738提高到0.943,相当于7个有效类别中约1.4个额外有效类别;贡献类覆盖率同样从0.370提高到0.425. 因此,该模型不仅产生更原始的建议,而且还产生更广泛的研究范式和贡献类型。

blocks.en: Diversity is also sensitive to early exploration. Removing serendipitous action swaps reduces paradigm coverage by 0.099, or roughly 0.7 effective categories, and contribution coverage by 0.067, or roughly 0.5 categories. This pattern is consistent with early exposure to less familiar behaviors helping the policy discover a broader set of useful trajectories.
blocks.zh: 多样性对早期探索也很敏感。 取消意外行动交换将范式覆盖面减少0.099, 或约0.7个有效类别, 捐款覆盖面减少0.067, 或约0.5个类别。 这种模式与早期接触不太熟悉的行为,帮助政策发现一套更广泛的有用轨迹是一致的.

blocks.en: The improvements are also not concentrated in a small set of CS topics. Night-8B improves over zero-shot Qwen3-8B on both citation and originality across all 36 evaluated domains, including healthcare, biomedical engineering, geosciences, and quantum science. Full per-domain results are provided in Appendix C .
blocks.zh: 改进工作也不集中在一套小的CS专题上. Night-8B在引用和原创性方面改进了零镜头的Qwen3-8B,涵盖所有36个评价领域,包括保健、生物医学工程、地球科学和量子科学。 每个领域的全部结果见附录C。

blocks.en: 4.4.3 Process Rewards Favor Originality over Breadth
blocks.zh: 4.4.3 优于面包的原创性

blocks.en: Table 3 (c) shows a different effect from directly rewarding the reasoning process. For Night-8B , process + outcome training raises originality by 5.29 points but lowers predicted citation impact by 3.69 points. Paradigm and contribution coverage also fall by roughly 0.6 and 0.4 effective categories, respectively. Process supervision can therefore favor more original individual proposals without necessarily producing a broader or more impactful set of ideas.
blocks.zh: 表3(c)显示与直接奖励推理过程不同的效果。 对于Night-8B,过程+结果训练提高了5.29分的原创性,但将预测的引用效果降低了3.69分. 参比率和贡献率也分别下降了约0.6和0.4有效类别。 因此,程序监督可以倾向于更原始的单个提案,而不一定产生更广泛或更具影响力的一套想法。

blocks.en: This effect is specific to the creativity-aligned action space. Adding the same process reward to ReAct sharply reduces both citation and originality, while Temperature also declines on both metrics. Process supervision is therefore not uniformly beneficial; its effect depends on whether the action space provides semantically distinct ways to express different degrees of creativity. We consequently use outcome-only training as our primary setting and treat process rewards as a way to shift the model toward greater proposal-level originality. We detail further analysis of P po P_{\texttt{po}} in Appendix 4.4.6 .
blocks.zh: 这种效果是针对创造力相配合的行动空间的。 在ReAct中加入同样的过程奖励会大幅降低引用和原创性,而温度在两种度量上也会下降. 因此,过程监督并非统一有益;其影响取决于行动空间是否提供了表现不同程度创造力的明显不同的方式。 因此,我们把只注重结果的培训作为我们的首要设定,并将进程奖励视为一种途径,将模式转向更大的建议层面的独创性。 我们进一步详细分析附录4.4.6中的P po P_{\textt{po}}。

blocks.en: 4.4.5 Semantic Creativity Levels Better Align with Output Behavior
blocks.zh: 4.4.5 语义创意水平与产出行为更好地保持一致

blocks.en: Our creativity levels are intended to change how an action is executed, not merely label it. Figure 3 measures this relationship using output entropy and semantic similarity (Appendix N ). AI Night-Scientist (PO) improves on both measures during training, while Temp (PO) deteriorates toward − 0.9 -0.9 . Semantic descriptions therefore provide a more learnable link between the selected creativity level and resulting behavior than temperature alone.
blocks.zh: 我们的创造力水平旨在改变一个行动是如何执行的,而不仅仅是标注它。 图3 使用输出 en和语义相似度量这种关系(附录N ). AI 夜间科学家在培训期间改进了这两项措施,而Time(PO)则恶化至-0.9-0.9。 因此,语义描述在选定的创造水平和由此产生的行为之间提供了比单独温度更能学习的联系.

blocks.en: 4.4.6 Process Rewards Shift the Learned Action Policy
blocks.zh: 4.4.6 过程奖励转移经验教训行动政策

blocks.en: Figure 4: Test-time action frequencies across five reasoning turns for three model variants.
blocks.zh: 图4:测试时间动作频率跨越5个推理转折,用于3个模型变体.

blocks.en: Figure 4 shows how the learned policies differ at test time. GPT-4.1 typically follows a short search → \rightarrow write → \rightarrow stop pattern, while Qwen3-8B-Base uses a broader mix of actions across the full trajectory. AI Night-Scientist-8B trained with process+outcome rewards shows a different preference: it selects spark more frequently across turns and tends to use it at moderate-to-high creativity levels. This suggests that process supervision shifts the policy toward assumption-challenging actions that more directly open new research directions.
blocks.zh: 图4显示在试验时学到的政策有何不同。 GPT-4.1一般遵循短搜索 ^\右手写 →\右手写 →\右手写 停止模式,而Quen3-8B-Base则使用跨整个轨迹的更广泛的动作组合. AI Night-Scientist-8B接受过过程+结果奖励的训练,显示出不同的偏好:它更频繁地选择交替的火花,并倾向于在中高创作水平上使用. 这表明,程序监督将政策转向更直接开启新研究方向的质疑假设的行动。

blocks.en: Debate is selected relatively rarely. One practical reason may be that it requires more of the trajectory budget, since the agent first identifies participants and relevant evidence before generating the grounded discussion. In general, this suggests that the learned value of an action depends not only on its creative potential, but also on how efficiently it contributes within a limited reasoning horizon.
blocks.zh: 辩论的选择相对较少。 一个实际原因可能是它需要更多的轨迹预算,因为代理人首先确定参与者和相关的证据,然后才进行有根据的讨论。 一般而言,这表明,一项行动所学到的价值不仅取决于其创造潜力,而且取决于它在有限推理范围内如何有效作出贡献。

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We introduce AI Night-Scientist , a creativity-aligned agentic framework that represents creativity at the action, process, and outcome levels and uses reinforcement learning to teach models when and how to depart from predictable reasoning. Applied to long-horizon research proposal generation, AI Night-Scientist improves predicted citation impact and originality by up to 32.03 and 66.15 points over its base model, while producing a broader range of research paradigms. These gains are not reproduced by higher decoding temperature or ReAct alone, supporting our central finding that creativity is more than sampling stochasticity. Our ablations further show that outcome-only training provides the strongest overall balance of quality and diversity, while process-level rewards can increase originality at the cost of citation impact and breadth. Together, these results suggest that creativity can be learned as a multi-level reasoning capability, enabling scientific agents to move more flexibly between the structured reasoning of day science and the exploratory reasoning of night science while remaining tools for human-led discovery.
blocks.zh: 我们介绍AI Night-Scientist,这是一个创造性的结合剂框架,它代表行动、进程和结果层面的创造性,并利用强化学习来教导模型何时以及如何偏离可预测的推理。 AI Night-Scientist应用到长视研究建议书生成中,将预测的引用影响和独创性比其基础模型提高了高达32.03分和66.15分,同时产生了更广泛的研究范式. 这些收益并非仅靠较高的解码温度或ReAct来复制,支持了我们的核心结论,即创造力不仅仅是取样的花样。 我们的总结进一步表明,只注重结果的培训在质量和多样性方面提供了最强有力的总体平衡,而进程层面的奖励可以增加独创性,而忽略引用的影响和广度。 这些结果表明,创造性可以作为一种多层次的推理能力来学习,使科学代理人能够更加灵活地在白天科学的结构推理和夜间科学的探索性推理之间移动,而同时又是人类主导的发现工具.

blocks.en: Ethics Statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en: AI Night-Scientist is designed for early-stage scientific ideation, when research directions are still speculative and not yet fully testable. Its role is to help researchers explore a broader set of possible directions, including connections or assumptions they may not otherwise consider. The system is intended as a creative collaborator rather than an autonomous researcher: generated proposals should be treated as candidate ideas that require critical evaluation, refinement, and validation by domain experts before they can support scientific conclusions.
blocks.zh: AI Night-Scientist是为早期科学思想而设计的,当时研究方向仍然具有推测性,尚不能完全测试. 其作用是帮助研究人员探索更广泛的可能方向,包括他们可能不考虑的联系或假设. 该系统的用意是作为一个创造性的合作者,而不是一个自主的研究者:生成的建议应当作为候选的想法对待,需要域专家的批判性评价,完善和验证才能支持科学结论.

blocks.en: Human ideation is often shaped by the concepts and examples already available in their local research community ( Lubart, 2001 ) . By encouraging proposals that depart from existing work while remaining relevant and feasible, AI Night-Scientist aims to surface directions beyond those most immediately accessible to a researcher or model. This may be especially useful for interdisciplinary exploration, where relevant ideas can be distributed across distant literature and research communities. Importantly, broader exploration does not imply that unfamiliar ideas are inherently better; their scientific value must still be established through expert judgment and empirical validation.
blocks.zh: 人类思想往往由当地研究界已有的概念和实例决定(Lubart,2001年)。 AI Night-Scientist通过鼓励那些脱离现有工作同时又仍然具有相关性和可行性的建议,力求在研究人员或模型最能立即获取的方向之外,展示方向。 这对跨学科探索可能特别有用,因为相关的想法可以传播到遥远的文献和研究界。 重要的是,更广泛的探索并不意味着不熟悉的想法本身就更好;其科学价值仍必须通过专家判断和经验验证确定。

blocks.en: As with other generative systems for scientific writing, AI Night-Scientist can produce plausible but incorrect, infeasible, or insufficiently grounded proposals, and could be misused to generate low-quality scientific content at scale. Its outputs should therefore be presented as AI-generated suggestions rather than validated research plans. Responsible use requires transparent disclosure, independent verification of claims and citations, and meaningful human oversight before ideas are pursued, disseminated, or incorporated into scientific work.

blocks.en: We select NSF CSE awards from 2018 onwards. Non-research grants (e.g., travel and conference grants) are excluded. blocks.en: To characterize the topical breadth of the training set, we applied an automated three-stage taxonomy pipeline to the 4,414 NSF award titles. In the first stage, GPT-4.1 assigned one to three fine-grained research subfields to each title in batches of 50, yielding 11,071 raw subfield labels (2.5 per title on average) spanning 4,300 unique terms. In the second stage, these labels were grouped into intermediate clusters via a second LLM pass. In the third stage, the intermediate clusters were consolidated into a final canonical taxonomy of 46 research domains (Table 6 ).
blocks.zh: 为了描述培训的热门范围,我们在4 414个NSF奖项上采用了自动的三阶段分类管道。 在第一阶段,GPT-4.1分批将1至3个细纹研究子场分给每个标题,分批50个,产生11,071个原始子场标签(平均每个标题2.5个),跨越4,300个独特的术语. 在第二阶段,这些标签通过第二个LM传球被分组为中间集群. 在第三阶段,中间集群被合并为由46个研究领域组成的最终犬科分类学(表6)。

blocks.en: The distribution reflects the intended scope of the NSF CISE directorate: Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning accounts for 23.1% of all subfield label occurrences, followed by Computer Science Theory (11.2%) and Networks & Communications (5.9%). The concentration in core CS and engineering is expected, especially as open-access literature on arXiv is most comprehensive for these fields, making retrieval-grounded proposal generation most reliable there. Importantly, the training set is not exclusively CS-focused: the remaining ∼ \sim 20% of labels span applied and interdisciplinary domains, including Biomedical Engineering & Health Informatics (2.7%), Cognitive & Behavioral Sciences (2.2%), Earth & Geosciences (1.0%), Quantum Science & Engineering (0.9%), and policy-adjacent areas such as Ethics, Equity & Societal Impacts and Economics, Policy & Law , providing a diverse training signal across 46 domains in total.

blocks.en: Table 8: Qualitative comparison for the NSF topic “Using AI to Transform Online Video Lectures.”

blocks.en: We qualitatively compare proposals on the NSF topic “Using Artificial Intelligence to Transform Online Video Lectures into Effective and Inclusive Agent-Based Presentations.” GPT-4.1 produces a well-structured but generic proposal that restates existing approaches (e.g., lecture segmentation and conversational agents) without introducing a distinguishing mechanism. ReAct adds a concrete multimodal engagement score but leaves its reinforcement learning formulation underspecified. AI Night-Scientist-8B (outcome-only) introduces the novel Agentify concept—treating lectures as live, co-created sessions in which an AI agent interleaves questions and dialogues in real time, rather than optimizing pre-recorded content after the fact. The process-reward variant proposes Progressive Content Enactors (PCEs), which deliberately introduce controlled errors and ambiguities into lectures to force students to actively resolve them (analogous to how working through a flawed proof teaches more than reading a perfect one), though its background section overreaches with unverifiable metrics. Table 8 provides excerpts and error analysis; key novel or well-specified contributions are highlighted in green , while vague, incremental, or questionable claims are highlighted in red .

ReAct增加了具体的多式联运参与得分,但未对其强化学习表述作出明确规定。 AI Night-Scientist-8B(仅以结果为主)介绍了小说Agentify概念——将讲座视为现场,共同创建的会话,在会话中,AI的代理人实时地进行提问和对话,而不是在事后优化预先录制的内容. 过程奖励的变式提出了累进内容发布者(PCEs),该变式有意在讲座中引入可控错误和含糊不清,以迫使学生积极解决这些问题(关于如何通过有缺陷的证明来工作比阅读一个完美的证明更能教人),尽管其背景部分用无法验证的衡量标准过度了。 表8提供了摘录和错误分析;主要的新颖或具体贡献以绿色突出,而模糊、递增或有疑问的索赔则以红色突出。

Below we document the core prompt structure and output schema for each creativity-enabled action ( search , debate , spark ) and the write action.

blocks.en: The search action generates up to five arXiv search queries. The creativity level controls query relevance: level 1 produces tightly targeted queries derived from proposal keywords; level 5 produces broad, exploratory queries spanning alternate domains, philosophical perspectives, or unrelated fields. Retrieved papers are parsed and appended to the trajectory context for use by subsequent actions.
blocks.zh: 搜索动作生成最多五个arXiv搜索查询. 创意级控制查询关联性:第1级产生来自提案关键词的严格定向查询;第5级产生涵盖其他域,哲学视角,或无关域的广泛,探索性查询. 获取的论文被解析,并附在轨迹上下文中,供以后的行动使用.

blocks.en: You are a researcher starting a literature review for a research proposal. Generate specific search queries whose relevance depends on the creativity level (1--5): Level 1 : Extremely relevant; queries based on terms from the proposal title. Level 2 : Very relevant; background and related works closely tied to the proposal. Level 3 : Somewhat relevant; tangentially related background. Level 4 : Loosely related; broader topics that still provide useful context. Level 5 : Very distantly relevant; alternate domains, perspectives, or philosophical questions. Problem: {problem} Level: {level} ( {level_description} ) Output JSON: {"search_queries": ["<query 1>", ..., "<query 5>"]}
blocks.zh: 你是一个研究者 开始一个文学评论 一个研究建议。 生成特定搜索查询,其相关性取决于创意级别(1-5): 第一级:极其相关;根据提案标题中的条款进行查询。 第二级:非常相关;背景和相关工作与提案密切相关。 3级:有一定关联性;有微小关联的背景. 4级:关系密切;范围较广,仍提供有用的背景。 第5级:非常遥远的相关;替代领域、观点或哲学问题。 问题: [问题] 级别 : {级别} ({级别_描述}) 输出 JSON : {"search_queries": ["<query 1>,......,"<query 5>]]]

blocks.en: F.2 Debate Action
blocks.zh: F.2 辩论行动

blocks.en: The debate action is executed in two sequential steps: (i) generating a debate setup (participants, topics, and structure) and (ii) simulating the debate conversation. The creativity level controls participant diversity and discussion structure, ranging from a focused single-turn discussion with a same-field colleague (level 1) to an open-ended, multi-turn panel with cross-disciplinary experts (level 5). The conversation is appended verbatim to the trajectory context.
blocks.zh: 辩论行动分两个顺序步骤进行:(一) 形成辩论安排(参与者、专题和结构)和(二) 模拟辩论对话。 创造性水平控制着参与者的多样性和讨论结构,从与同一领域同事(第1级)进行有重点的单回合讨论到由多学科专家(第5级)组成的不限成员名额多回合小组。 对话逐字附在轨迹上下文。

blocks.en: Step 1 --- Debate Setup. You are a researcher designing a debate. The creativity level controls who you debate with, what topics you cover, and how the debate is structured: Level 1 : Single senior colleague in the same area; structured single-turn debate on proposal specifics. Level 2 : Peer on related topics; structured, focused on the proposal with minor deviation. Level 3 : Peer from the same field but a different topic; open-ended multi-turn, some deviation allowed. Level 4 : Domain-expert from a different discipline or a 2--3 expert panel; open-ended, broader scope. Level 5 : Expert(s) from a completely different discipline; unstructured, high-level philosophical exploration. Problem: {problem} Level: {level} Output JSON: {"debate_participants": [{"name": "...", "job": "...", "expertise": "..."}], "debate_topics": ["..."], "debate_structure": "..."}
blocks.zh: 步骤1 -- -- 辩论设置。 你是设计辩论的研究员 创意水平控制着您与谁辩论,您涉及哪些议题,以及辩论的结构: 第1级:同一领域的单身高级同事;关于提案细节的结构化单回合辩论。 第2级:相关专题的同行;结构化,侧重于稍有偏差的提案. 第三级:来自同一字段但主题不同的对等点;可开放的多回合,允许一些偏差. 4级:来自不同学科或2-3专家小组的域专家;范围不限,范围更广. 第5级:来自完全不同学科的专家;无结构,高层次的哲学探索. 问题: [问题] 级别: {级别}输出 JSON: {'debate_particies': {{{'名称:"...","工作": "...","专家":"},"辩论_专题":[...],"辩论_结构":"}

blocks.en: Step 2 --- Debate Conversation. You are a researcher conducting the debate as set up above. Generate a coherent, multi-turn conversation where each participant draws on their specific expertise with concrete details. Responses should not be surface level. Debate setup: {debate_setup} Output JSON: {"conversation_history": [{"speaker_name": "...", "speaker_response": "..."}]}
blocks.zh: 步骤2 -- -- 辩论对话。 您是一位研究者,主持上述辩论。 产生一个连贯的、多回合的对话,使每个参与者利用他们的具体专门知识,并有具体的细节。 答复不应是表面水平。 辩论设置 : {debate_setup} 输出 JSON : {"论语_历史" : [{"论语_名称":"...,"论语_回应":"...}]]

blocks.en: F.3 Spark Action
blocks.zh: F.3 火花行动

blocks.en: The spark action generates a “Bit-Flip” idea ( O’Neill et al., 2025 ) : it inverts a commonly held assumption to produce a novel research direction. The creativity level governs the scope of the challenged assumption, from a specific proposal-level constraint (level 1) to a field-reshaping paradigm shift (level 5). The Bit-Flip is appended to the trajectory context and can influence subsequent write and action-selection steps.
blocks.zh: 火花动作产生一个"Bit-Flip"(O ' Neill et al., 2025)的想法:它颠倒了一个通常持有的假设来产生一个新的研究方向. 创造性层面制约着被质疑的假设的范围,从具体的建议书层面的制约(第1级)到实地调整范式的转变(第5级)。 Bit-Flip附着在轨迹上下文,可以影响后续的写和动作选择步骤.

blocks.en: You are a researcher who has just had a sudden insight that challenges conventional thinking. Generate a Bit-Flip: identify a prevailing belief in the field (the Bit ), invert or challenge it (the Flip ), and distill the core conceptual leap into a single phrase (the Spark ). Creativity level controls the scope: Level 1 : Minor, proposal-specific assumption to challenge. Level 2 : Minor but somewhat broader assumption; questions existing approaches in the proposal. Level 3 : Moderate assumption; meaningful challenge to existing norms within the proposal. Level 4 : Significant, field-level assumption; substantial departure from the status quo. Level 5 : Major, paradigm-level assumption; potential to revolutionize the field. Problem: {problem} Level: {level} Output JSON: {"bit": "<2--3 sentences on the status quo and its limitation>", "flip": "<novel approach or perspective, ≥ \geq 2 sentences>", "spark": "<core phrase>"}
blocks.zh: 你是一个研究者,他刚刚有 突然的洞察力,挑战 常规思维。 生成 Bit-Flip : 识别在球场(the Bit)中流行的信念,反转或挑战(the Flip ),并将核心概念跳跃分馏为单个短语(the Spark ). 创意级别控制范围 : 1级:小的,针对具体提案的假设以提出质疑. 第二级:略微但范围较广的假设;质疑提案中的现有办法。 第三级:适度假设;对提案内现有规范提出有意义的挑战。 第4级:重大、外地一级的假设;与现状大不相同。 5级:主要,范式级假设;具有革命化领域的潜力. 问题: [问题] 级别: {level} 输出 JSON: {"bit": "关于现状及其限制的<2-3句子>", "flip": "<novel 方法或视角,\\ geq 2 句子>", "spark": "<核心短语>>"}

blocks.en: F.4 Write Action
blocks.zh: F.4 写作

blocks.en: The write action produces or revises the complete structured proposal. It takes all accumulated trajectory context as input and outputs a structured JSON proposal. The creativity level is fixed at 1 for this action; creative expression is instead encoded in the trajectory that feeds into it.
blocks.zh: 写作动作产生或修改完整的结构化建议. 它将所有累积的轨迹背景作为投入和产出结构化的JSON建议。 创作级别被固定为此动作的1级;反之,创作表达方式被编码在输入它的轨迹中.

blocks.en: You are a researcher writing or revising a research proposal based on all information gathered throughout the writing process. Create a coherent, comprehensive proposal. You may deviate from prior ideas if it improves the proposal. Problem: {problem} Current proposal: {proposal} Context history: {context} Output JSON: {"proposal_title": "...", "proposal_summary": "concise statement of what, why, and what problems it resolves", "background_and_significance": "historical review of the field, what remains to be done, and how this proposal advances it", "research_plan": [{"phase": "...", "idea": "detailed hypothesis and contribution", "experimental_plan": "concrete methods, evaluation, pitfalls, fallback plans"}]}
blocks.zh: 您是一位研究者,根据整个写作过程中收集的所有信息撰写或修订研究提案. 制定一个连贯、全面的建议。 如果改进了提案,你可能会偏离以前的想法。 问题: [问题] 目前的建议: {提议} 背景历史 : { context} 产出 JSON: {"提案_标题":"...","提案_摘要":"关于它解决什么,为什么,什么问题的简明说明","背景_和_标志":"对领域的历史回顾,还有什么工作,以及这个建议如何推进","研究_计划":[{"阶段":"......,"理想":"详细假设和贡献","实验_计划":"具体方法,评价,陷阱,倒背计划"}}}

blocks.en: Appendix G SciJudge Evaluation Details
blocks.zh: 附录G 法官 评价细节

blocks.en: We evaluate proposal quality using SciJudge (OpenMOSS-Team/SciJudge-30B) ( Tong et al., 2026 ) , a 30B-parameter model trained to predict scientific impact via citation forecasting. For each problem instance in the test set, we compare a model-generated proposal against a matched reconstructed reference NSF proposal in a pairwise setting.
blocks.zh: 我们使用Sci Judge(OpenMOSS-Team/Sci Judge-30B)(Tong等人,2026年)来评价提案的质量,这是经过培训的30B参数模型,通过引用预测来预测科学影响。 对于测试集中的每个问题实例,我们比较一个模型生成的提案,与一个匹配的重构参考NSF的提案在对齐的环境下进行比较.

blocks.en: Today is {date} . Based on the titles and abstracts of the following two proposals A and B, determine which proposal has a higher citation count across its eventual papers. {timing_assumption} (e.g., ‘‘Assume Proposal B was published earlier than Proposal A.’’) Show your reasoning process in <reason> </reason> tags. Return the final answer in <answer> </answer> tags. The final answer should contain only ‘A’ or ‘B’. Proposal A: Title: {title_a} Abstract: {abstract_a} Proposal B: Title: {title_b} Abstract: {abstract_b}
blocks.zh: 今天是{日期}。 根据以下两项提案A和B的标题和摘要,确定哪项提案在最终文件中的引用次数较高。 {估计_假设}(例如,`假定提案B'比提议A.___早发布) 在“ reason” 标签中显示您的推理进程。 返回在 < answer > </ answer > 标签中的最后答案。 最后的答案应只包含‘A'或‘B'. 建议A:标题:{标题_a}摘要:{摘要_a}提议B:标题:{标题_b}摘要:{摘要_b}

blocks.en: Randomized A/B order. For each pair, proposal order is randomized using a deterministic per-pair seed to eliminate position bias. The model does not know which proposal originated from the system under evaluation versus the reconstructed reference.
blocks.zh: 随机A/B顺序. 每对标本的标本顺序采用确定性每帕种子来随机排列,以消除位置偏差. 该模式并不知道从评价中的系统得出哪些建议,而参考的则是重建的。

blocks.en: Temporal framing. When comparing against the synthetically reconstructed proposal (Appendix K ), we instruct the judge to assume the reconstructed reference proposal was published earlier . This grounds the comparison in a realistic temporal context: the model-generated proposal is treated as the “newer” proposal, which must surpass the quality of the funded reference to be preferred.
blocks.zh: 时间框架 与合成重建提案(Appendix K)相比,我们指示法官假定重建后的参考提案早些发表. 这为在现实的时间背景下进行比较提供了理由:模型生成的建议书被视为“新”建议书,它必须超过所选择的获得资金的参考的质量。

blocks.en: Output parsing. The model responds with chain-of-thought reasoning inside <reason>...</reason> tags and a final answer (A or B) inside <answer>...</answer> tags. We extract the answer tag; if absent or malformed, we fall back to a regex match on the first standalone ‘A’ or ‘B’ character.
blocks.zh: 输出剖析. 该模型在 " 解释 " ... " / " 解释 " 标记内用思维链推理和在 " 回答 " ... " / " 回答 " 标记内用最后答案(A或B)。 我们提取解答标记; 如果缺失或结构不当, 我们回到第一个独立“ A” 或“ B” 字符的正则匹配 。

blocks.en: We report pairwise win rate: the fraction of evaluated pairs for which SciJudge predicts the model-generated proposal to yield greater downstream citation impact than the matched reconstructed reference.
blocks.zh: 我们报告双向胜率:Sci Judge预测模型产生的建议所评估的对对对对的引用效果大于相应重建的引用。

blocks.en: Appendix H Contribution-Type Classification Details
blocks.zh: 附录H 贡献-类型分类细节

blocks.en: We classify each proposal by its primary scholarly contribution using GPT-5.4-mini and a seven-way taxonomy adapted from Wobbrock (2012) . The contribution types are: empirical , which produces new findings from systematically gathered or analyzed data; artifact , which creates a novel instantiated system, tool, process, intervention, or other constructed artifact; methodological , which introduces or refines a reusable method; theoretical , which develops reusable concepts, models, principles, hypotheses, or frameworks; benchmark or dataset , which contributes a reusable data or evaluation resource; survey , which synthesizes existing work into higher-level understanding; and opinion , which advances an evidence-grounded position intended to persuade or redirect discussion.
blocks.zh: 我们用GPT-5.4-mini和从Wobbrock(2012年)改编的七行分类法, 贡献类型包括:经验性,从系统收集或分析的数据中得出新的结论;人工制品,创造新的即时系统、工具、过程、干预或其他人工制品;方法性,引入或完善可重复使用的方法;理论性,开发可重复使用的概念、模型、原则、假设或框架;基准或数据集,提供可重复使用的数据或评价资源;调查,将现有工作综合到更高层次的理解;意见性,提出以证据为依据的立场,旨在说服或重新引导讨论。

blocks.en: Distinction from research-idea paradigms. Contribution type captures what form of scholarly output the proposal ultimately contributes, whereas the research-idea paradigm captures what high-level research move is used to turn an opportunity into a proposed direction. Following the research-idea annotation setup of Chen et al. (2026) , our paradigm categories distinguish moves such as assumption relaxation, failure mitigation, formal derivation, empirical mapping, artifact construction, and optimization. The two axes are therefore complementary rather than redundant. For example, an artifact contribution may arise from relaxing an assumption, mitigating a failure, or optimizing resource use; conversely, a measurement-oriented research idea may ultimately contribute either empirical findings or a reusable benchmark.
blocks.zh: 与研究-思想范式的区别. 贡献类型包括建议最终贡献的学术产出形式,而研究-理想范式则包括利用高级别研究将机会转化为拟议方向。 在陈等人(2026年)的研究思想注解设置之后,我们的范式分类区分了假设放松,故障缓解,形式推导,经验制图,文物建造,优化等动作. 因此,这两个轴是相辅相成的,而不是多余的。 例如,减轻假设、减轻失败或优化资源利用可能带来一种人工的贡献;反之,以衡量为导向的研究想法可能最终促成经验性结论或可重复使用的基准。

blocks.en: Primary-label selection. The classifier is instructed to distinguish the proposal’s central contribution from methods or artifacts that merely support it. In particular, empirical contributions are defined by the new findings produced from data, while benchmark or dataset contributions are defined by the reusable resource itself. Similarly, artifact contributions center on a novel instantiated invention, whereas methodological contributions center on a reusable way of conducting research or practice. Theoretical contributions may be empirically evaluated, but the reusable concept, explanation, model, or framework must remain the principal contribution.
blocks.zh: 初标选择. 要求分类员将提案的中心贡献与仅仅支持该提案的方法或文物区分开来。 特别是,经验性贡献由数据产生的新结果界定,而基准或数据集贡献则由可重复使用的资源本身界定。 同样,文物贡献以新的即时发明为中心,而方法贡献则以可重复使用的研究或实践方式为中心。 理论贡献可按经验加以评价,但可重复使用的概念、解释、模式或框架必须仍然是主要贡献。

blocks.en: Reported diversity. For our diversity analysis, we use only the primary contribution label for each proposal. We measure how broadly and evenly a model distributes its proposals across the seven contribution types using the normalized effective number of categories described in Section 4.2 .
blocks.zh: 报告的多样性。 在我们进行多样性分析时,我们只使用每项建议的主要贡献标签。 我们用第4.2节所述的正常有效类别数目,衡量一个模式在七个捐款类别中如何广泛和平均地分配其建议。

blocks.en: Appendix I LLM Originality Evaluation Details
blocks.zh: 附录一 LLM 原始评价细节

blocks.en: System: You are an experienced NSF proposal reviewer. Return valid JSON only. User: You are a reviewer for NSF proposals who has been a professor in your field for over 20 years. You are comparing two proposals that address the same award problem. Judge which proposal is more original. Originality must be judged relative to: (1) the other proposal; (2) the closest retrieved paper for Proposal A; (3) the closest retrieved paper for Proposal B. If a proposal appears more novel at first glance but is very similar to its closest retrieved paper, penalize its novelty accordingly. Award title / target problem: {problem_title} Proposal A: {proposal_a} Closest Retrieved Paper for Proposal A: Title: {paper_a_title} Abstract: {paper_a_abstract} Proposal B: {proposal_b} Closest Retrieved Paper for Proposal B: Title: {paper_b_title} Abstract: {paper_b_abstract} Criteria: Originality of the central concepts; distance from the closest retrieved paper; whether the proposal goes beyond recombining familiar ideas; depth of novelty rather than superficial novelty; whether the proposal opens genuinely new technical directions. Calibration examples: • Borderline positive: Proposal A may look less flashy but introduces a genuinely different technical lever, representation, or problem decomposition than both Proposal B and A’s closest paper. • Borderline negative: Proposal A is polished but most apparent creativity comes from extending the closest paper to a new application or evaluation setting without a clearly new core idea. • Borderline negative: Proposal A combines familiar components into a multi-phase agenda; breadth alone is not novelty if the contribution is still an expected recombination of known methods. • Borderline negative: Do not reward writing sophistication, dense terminology, or detailed milestones if the underlying idea remains close to prior work. Return JSON only: {"winner": "A or B", "explanation": "brief comparative rationale"}
blocks.zh: System:你是一个有经验的NSF建议书审查员. 仅返回有效的 JSON 。 用户:您是NSF提案的审查者, 你们正在比较两个解决同一裁决问题的提案。 判断哪个建议更独创 判断原件时必须参照:(1) 另一提案;(2) 提案A的最近检索文件;(3) 提案B的最近检索文件。 如果一项提案乍看起来比较新颖,但与它最接近的检索文件非常相似,则应相应惩罚其新颖性。 奖牌/ 目标问题 : { problem_ title} A提案:{提议_a}A提案最接近检索的文件:标题:{文件_a_标题} 摘要 : {paper_a_a_抽象} 提议B:{提议_b} 关闭获取的提案 B 的纸张: 标题 : {paper_ b_ title} 摘要 : {paper_b_abstract} 标准: 中心概念的原创性; 与最近检索的文件的距离; 提案是否超出重新组合熟悉的想法; 新的深度而不是表面的新颖性; 提案是否开辟了真正的新的技术方向。 • 边界线正数: 提议 与提议B和A最接近的论文相比,A看起来可能不太闪烁,但引入了真正不同的技术杠杆、代表或问题分解。 • 支助 边线负数:提议 A被打磨,但最明显的创造力来自将最接近的纸张延伸至新的应用或评价环境,而没有明显新的核心思想。 • 支助 边线负数:提议 将熟悉的内容结合到一个多阶段的议程之中;如果这种贡献仍然是已知方法的预期重组,那么光是宽度就不是新颖的。 • 支助 边线负数 : 如果基本想法仍然接近先前的工作,则不奖励书写精密、术语繁杂或详细的里程碑。 返回 JSON 仅: {"胜者":"A或B","解释":"简单比较理由"]

blocks.en: Borderline positive: Proposal A may look less flashy but introduces a genuinely different technical lever, representation, or problem decomposition than both Proposal B and A’s closest paper.
blocks.zh: 边线正数 : 提议 与提议B和A最接近的论文相比,A看起来可能不太闪烁,但引入了真正不同的技术杠杆、代表或问题分解。

blocks.en: Borderline negative: Proposal A is polished but most apparent creativity comes from extending the closest paper to a new application or evaluation setting without a clearly new core idea.
blocks.zh: 边线负数:提议 A被打磨,但最明显的创造力来自将最接近的纸张延伸至新的应用或评价环境,而没有明显新的核心思想。

blocks.en: Borderline negative: Proposal A combines familiar components into a multi-phase agenda; breadth alone is not novelty if the contribution is still an expected recombination of known methods.
blocks.zh: 边线负数:提议 将熟悉的内容结合到一个多阶段的议程之中;如果这种贡献仍然是已知方法的预期重组,那么光是宽度就不是新颖的。

blocks.en: Borderline negative: Do not reward writing sophistication, dense terminology, or detailed milestones if the underlying idea remains close to prior work.
blocks.zh: 边线负数 : 如果基本想法仍然接近先前的工作,则不奖励书写精密、术语繁杂或详细的里程碑。

blocks.en: We assess Originality using GPT-5.1 as a judge in a pairwise setting. For each test instance, the model-generated proposal and the matched reconstructed reference proposal are each submitted to our arXiv retrieval system; the top-1 closest paper is retrieved for each using sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding-based search. The retrieval query is constructed from the proposal title concatenated with the first three sentences of the proposal summary. Proposal order (A vs. B) is randomized per-pair using a deterministic seed to eliminate position bias.

blocks.en: The judge is instructed to assess originality relative to both the competing proposal and the closest retrieved paper for each proposal. This prevents superficially creative proposals from scoring well if their core idea closely mirrors existing literature. The judgment emphasizes: (i) originality of the central concept, (ii) distance from the retrieved nearest neighbor, (iii) whether the proposal recombines familiar ideas or opens a genuinely new technical direction, and (iv) depth of novelty over breadth or terminological density.

blocks.zh: 我们报告对模型生成的建议书胜过相应参考的对数(模型胜率)。

blocks.en: Appendix J Human Evaluation Study
blocks.zh: 附录J 人类评价研究

blocks.en: To assess the reliability of our automated evaluation metrics, we conducted a small-scale human evaluation in which two expert annotators independently judged 33 pairwise proposal comparisons (covering all three model variants: Qwen3-8B-Base, GPT-4.1, and AI Night-Scientist-8B). Each item presented annotators with a model-generated proposal alongside a matched reconstructed reference proposal; annotators selected the preferred proposal on two axes (predicted citation impact and precedence) or indicated a tie. Both independent annotators have 5+ and 15+ years of research experience in related fields, respectively.
blocks.zh: 为了评估我们自动评价指标的可靠性,我们进行了一次小规模的人类评价,两名专家注释员独立判断了33项对等建议比较(涵盖所有三个模型变体:Qune3-8B-Base、GPT-4.1和AI Night-Scientist-8B)。 每个项目都向注释者提出了一份模型生成的提案,并附有一份相应的重构参考提案;注释者按两个轴线选择了首选提案(预计引文的影响和优先级),或表示相同。 两个独立的注释员分别在相关领域拥有5年以上和15年以上的研究经验.

blocks.en: J.1 Inter-Annotator Agreement
blocks.zh: J.1 书记员 协议

blocks.en: Table 10 reports inter-annotator agreement. Agreement is high on citation impact (80.0%, κ = 0.625 \kappa{=}0.625 , substantial) and originality (86.7%, κ = 0.766 \kappa{=}0.766 , substantial), indicating that both dimensions can be reliably assessed by domain-expert annotators.

blocks.en: J.2 Human-LLM Agreement
blocks.zh: J.2 人类-LLM 协议

blocks.en: We also measure how well the LLM judges (SciJudge for predicted citation impact, GPT-5.1 for originality) agree with human annotators. For each annotator response, we map the human A/B choice to a model or ground_truth winner using the answer key, and compare against the corresponding LLM judgment; ties and null LLM outputs are excluded. Table 11 reports the results pooled across both annotators.
blocks.zh: 我们还衡量LLM法官(预测引文影响的科学法官,GPT-5.1的独创性法官)与人类注释员的一致程度。 对于每个注释员的反应,我们用答案键将人类的A/B选择映射到一个模型或地面-真相胜者,并与相应的LLM判断进行比较;链接和无效LLM输出被排除在外. 表11汇报了两个报章员的汇总结果。

blocks.en: Table 11: Human-LLM agreement on predicted citation impact and originality. Ties and unparseable LLM outputs are excluded.
blocks.zh: 表11:人类-LLM关于预测引用影响和原创性的协议。 链接和无法分割的LLM输出被排除在外.

blocks.en: Agreement in the low-to-mid 70s is consistent with prior work reporting LLM-judge alignment with human raters ( Zheng et al., 2023 ) , and notably these human–LLM agreement rates provide additional evidence that the automated judges broadly track expert preferences at the proposal level. These results support the use of SciJudge and GPT-5.1 as scalable proxies for human judgment at the proposal level.

blocks.en: Appendix K Reconstructed Reference Proposal Construction
blocks.zh: 附录K 参考建议书

blocks.en: Original NSF grant proposals are not publicly available. We therefore construct reconstructed reference proposals from evidence surrounding each funded project. These reconstructions are not intended to reproduce the original proposal text; rather, they provide standardized, evidence-grounded references for research directions that were actually funded and subsequently pursued. The proposal-generating model never receives the award abstracts, project outcomes, or associated publications used in this reconstruction.
blocks.zh: 最初的NSF赠款建议并不公开。 因此,我们从每个供资项目的证据中重建了参考建议。 这些重建的目的不是要复制原提案案文,而是为实际获得资助并随后进行的研究方向提供标准化、有证据依据的参考。 产生建议书的模式从未收到这种重建中使用的授标摘要、项目结果或相关出版物。

blocks.en: 1. Collect award evidence. For each award, we collect its title, abstract, project outcomes report (POR), PI names, award ID, and award period from the NSF Awards Database. 2. Retrieve likely associated papers by PI. We use PI-first retrieval over arXiv, issuing up to 12 author-based queries using PI full names, surnames, and combinations of multiple PIs. Results are deduplicated by arXiv ID. This constrains retrieval to papers plausibly authored by the funded investigators before using topical information to determine which papers are most closely associated with the award. 3. Rank candidate papers using award evidence. Candidate papers are first ranked using PI-author overlap, topical overlap between the award evidence (title, abstract, and POR) and the paper title and abstract, and publication timing relative to the award period. We additionally reward cases in which the award title appears directly in the paper abstract. PI overlap receives the strongest weight so that topical similarity alone cannot make an unrelated paper a strong candidate. 4. Verify candidates using full-text evidence. For the highest-ranked candidates, we retrieve the paper text and extract the abstract, introduction, methods or approach, and experiments or results, excluding references and appendices where possible. We then rescore papers using full-text evidence, including explicit mention of the NSF award ID, NSF funding acknowledgments, PI surnames, and topical overlap with the award. We retain up to three highly ranked papers per award. If no paper passes the grounding threshold, we retain the strongest PI-matched papers with usable text so that reconstruction remains grounded in likely investigator-authored work. 5. Reconstruct a plausible pre-award research plan. We prompt GPT-5.1 as an expert NSF PI using the award metadata, POR, and selected papers. Crucially, the prompt treats publications as downstream evidence of what the funded project ultimately produced and asks the model to infer a plausible pre-award research plan that could have led to those outcomes, rather than summarize or copy the papers. The model is instructed not to mention the reconstruction process and to produce the same structured format used by our generated proposals: a proposal summary, background and significance, and a multi-phase research plan specifying the central idea and experimental plan for each phase.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 收集裁决证据。 对于每个奖项,我们从NSF奖项数据库收集其标题,抽象,项目成果报告(POR),PI名称,奖项ID,以及奖期. 2. 获取PI可能的相关论文. 我们使用 PI 的第一检索在 arXiv 之上, 发布多达12个基于作者的查询 使用 PI 的全名,姓氏,和多个 PI 的组合。 结果由arXiv ID复制. 这限制了在利用专题信息确定哪些文件与裁决最密切相关之前,检索由受资助调查员合理撰写的论文。 3. 利用授标证据对候选人论文进行排名。 候选人论文的排名首先采用PI-作者的重叠,在授标证据(标题,抽象和POR)与论文标题和抽象,以及相对于授标期的出版时间之间进行专题重叠. 我们进一步奖励在论文摘要中直接出现奖名的案例。 个人资料的重叠得到最强的份量,因此,仅凭专题上的相似性并不能使一份无关的论文成为强有力的候选人。 4. 利用全文证据核查候选人。 对于排名最高的候选人,我们检索文件文本,并摘录抽象、介绍、方法或方法,以及试验或结果,尽可能不提及参考和附录。 然后,我们再用全文证据撰写复古论文,包括明确提及NSF奖项ID、NSF资助确认、PI姓氏以及与该奖项的专题重叠。 我们每个奖项保留了多达三篇高档论文. 如果没有纸能越过地面阈值,我们保留最强的具有可用文本的PI比对文件,以便重建工作仍然以可能由调查人员撰写的工作为基础。 5. 重建一项可行的授标前研究计划。 我们利用奖项元数据、POR和一些论文, 关键的是,立即将出版物视为资助项目最终产出的下游证据,并要求模型推断出一个可以导致这些成果的可信的授标前研究计划,而不是总结或复制论文。 指示该模式不要提及重建进程,而要提出我们提出的提案所用的同样结构化的格式:提案摘要、背景和意义,以及一个多阶段研究计划,其中具体说明每个阶段的中心想法和实验计划。

blocks.en: Appendix L Process-Level Reward Details
blocks.zh: 附录L 流程级奖励细节

blocks.en: The process-level reward evaluates the quality of the agent’s reasoning trajectory rather than only its final output. Each intermediate action (i.e., all actions before the final write ) is scored along two complementary dimensions: exploration and contribution . Both scores are produced by an LLM judge, mapped from the 1–5 integer scale to [ − 1 , 1 ] [-1,1] via the centering transform s ′ = ( s − 3 ) / 2 s^{\prime}=(s-3)/2 , and averaged equally into a per-action score. The overall process reward is the mean of all per-action scores; actions that were available but unused (i.e., the trajectory is shorter than the maximum allowed) are penalized with a score of − 1 -1 .
blocks.zh: 过程级奖励评价代理商推理轨迹的质量,而不仅仅是其最终产出. 每个中间行动(即最后写作前的所有行动)按两个相辅相成的方面打分:勘探和贡献。 两个分数均由LLM裁判产生,通过中转s=(s−3)/2 s^{\prime}=(s−3)/2,从1–5整数比例图绘制为[−1,1] [-1,1],平均为每个动作分数. 整个过程的奖励是所有按动作计分的平均值;可用但未使用的动作(即轨迹短于允许的最大)将受到−1-1的处罚.

blocks.en: L.1 Exploration Scoring
blocks.zh: L.1 勘探测量

blocks.en: The exploration dimension rewards actions that cover genuinely new ground relative to everything already explored in the trajectory. A high exploration score indicates that the action introduces a novel direction, perspective, or information source that prior actions did not cover; a low score indicates redundancy. If no prior actions have been taken, the action is considered maximally exploratory by default.
blocks.zh: 与轨道上已经探索的一切相比,勘探层面奖励了涵盖真正新地面的行动。 高勘探分数表明,该动作引入了前作未涵盖的新方向,视角或信息来源;低分数表示冗余. 如果事先没有采取行动,则认为这一行动默认是最大限度的探索。

blocks.en: L.2 Contribution Scoring
blocks.zh: L.2 贡献分数

blocks.en: The contribution dimension rewards actions that meaningfully shaped the final proposal’s quality. Each intermediate action is scored for how much it contributed to the final proposal’s precedence, feasibility, and overall quality, conditioned on prior actions (to avoid rewarding redundant actions that happen to echo an earlier high-value contribution).
blocks.zh: 贡献方面奖励了影响最后提案质量的行动。 每个中间行动都因其对最后提案的优先地位、可行性和整体质量的贡献程度而得分,而最终提案是以先前的行动为条件的(以避免重复先前的高价值贡献的重复行动)。

blocks.en: You are a reviewer for NSF proposals who has been a professor in your field for over 20 years. Evaluate whether the current action is sufficiently different and novel compared to previous actions in the research process. Problem statement: {problem} Current action type: {action_type} Current action output: {action_output} Prior actions taken (ordered): {previous_actions} Assess how meaningfully different the current action is from the previous actions. Consider: • Does it explore a new direction or perspective not previously covered? • Would it provide substantially different information from prior actions? • For search : are the queries fundamentally different from prior queries or debate topics? • For debate : are the topics/participants substantially different from prior debates? • For spark : does it challenge different assumptions than prior spark actions? Assign a low score if this action would likely generate outputs similar to prior actions; assign a high score if it explores genuinely new ground. Score from 1 to 5: 1 = Not exploratory; highly redundant with prior actions. 2 = Slightly exploratory; mostly overlaps with prior actions. 3 = Moderately exploratory; some new perspectives with limited novelty. 4 = Very exploratory; covers substantially new ground. 5 = Highly exploratory; genuinely novel direction with minimal overlap. Output JSON: {"score": <int>, "explanation": "<string>"}

blocks.en: You are a reviewer for NSF proposals who has been a professor in your field for over 20 years. Evaluate how much a single intermediate action contributed to the final proposal across three dimensions: precedence, feasibility, and overall quality. Problem statement: {problem} Final proposal: {final_proposal} Prior actions before this one (ordered): {previous_actions} Intermediate action type: {action_type} Intermediate action output: {action_output} When scoring, condition on prior actions. If this action mostly repeats prior actions with similar outputs, assign low contribution scores. blocks.en: During training, we track two diagnostic metrics, action-level entropy and action-level similarity , that measure whether the model’s actual output behavior is consistent with its selected creativity level. Neither metric is used as a reward signal; they serve purely as interpretability probes.
blocks.zh: 在训练期间,我们追踪两个诊断度量,即动作层面的 en和动作层面的相似性,用来测量模型的实际输出行为是否与其选定的创造水平一致. 两个度量衡都不用作奖励信号;它们纯粹是可解释性探测器。

blocks.en: The core premise of our creativity-aligned framework is that selecting a higher creativity level should demonstrably change how the model acts, producing outputs with higher token entropy (more lexical variety) and outputs that are more distinct from the evolving proposal (higher divergence). If a model selects level 5 but generates outputs indistinguishable from level 1, the creativity selector is decorative rather than functional. These metrics operationalize that sanity check.
blocks.zh: 我们的创造力协调框架的核心前提是,选择更高的创造力水平应明显地改变模型的操作方式,产生具有更高象征式的py(更古典化的品种)和与不断演变的提案(更大的差异)更为不同的产出。 如果一个模型选择第5级,但生成输出与第1级无法区分,则创意选择器是装饰性的而不是功能性的. 这些度量衡可以运行 理智检查。

blocks.en: For each action, we collect the per-token log-probabilities from the model’s generation and compute the mean Shannon entropy across top- k k vocabulary candidates. This is averaged over all tokens in the action output to yield a single per-action entropy score. We then compute the Pearson correlation between the action’s selected creativity level (equivalently, its inverse noise level 1 − noise / max_level 1-\text{noise}/\text{max\_level} ) and this entropy value across all actions in a training batch. A positive correlation indicates that higher creativity levels lead to higher-entropy, more diverse token distributions.
blocks.zh: 每一次行动,我们都会从模型的生成中收集每端的对数概率,并计算出横跨顶端-k k 词汇的平均值。 这在动作输出中的所有符号上均值,以产生单个的每个动作的 en分. 然后我们计算动作选定创造性水平(相当于其反向噪音水平1 - 噪音 / 最大_ text{noise}/\text{max{level})与训练批次中所有行动中的这个等值之间的皮尔逊关联。 正面的关联性表明,更高的创造水平会导致更高的内涵,更多样化的代币分布.

blocks.en: For each action, we compute the cosine similarity between the action output’s sentence embedding and the embedding of the most recently written proposal draft (or the problem statement if no draft exists yet). We again compute the Pearson correlation between the creativity level and this similarity score across the batch. A negative correlation (similarity decreases as creativity level increases) is desirable: higher creativity should yield actions that cover genuinely new territory rather than paraphrasing what has already been written.

blocks.en: Appendix O Limitations
blocks.zh: 附录O 限制

blocks.en: Training creativity-aligned agents requires substantial GPU compute. We mitigate this by working with an efficient 8B-parameter architecture, but scaling to larger models would amplify the footprint. Additionally, our reward pipeline relies on LLM judges (GPT-4.1 for feasibility/relevance during training, SciJudge-30B and GPT-5.1 for evaluation). Unlike similarity-based reward signals that compare generated text against existing corpora, we deliberately use LLM judges to assess genuinely new ideas—minimizing data leakage and preventing the model from learning to simply paraphrase known work from our dataset, which spans proposals as far back as 2018. This design choice comes at higher inference cost but is central to the validity of the precedence and originality signal.
blocks.zh: 培训与创造力相适应的代理人需要大量的GPU计算. 我们通过一个高效的8B参数架构来缓解这种情况,但缩小到更大的模型将扩大足迹。 此外,我们的奖励程序依靠LLM法官(GPT-4.1用于培训期间的可行性/相关性,SciJudge-30B和GPT-5.1用于评估)。 与以相似性为基础的奖励信号比较生成的文本与现有的corpora不同,我们有意使用LLM判断来评估真正的新想法——尽量减少数据泄漏,防止模型学习从我们的数据集中简单地诠释已知的工作,该数据集跨越了早在2018年的提案. 这种设计选择以较高的推论成本来进行,但对优先和原创性信号的有效性至关重要.

blocks.en: Given the inherent complexity of our task, particularly the implicit objective of increasing the entropy of a model’s outputs, we have observed that training can become unstable, especially over longer training runs. High-entropy generation is at odds with the stability assumptions underlying standard RL algorithms designed for low-variance, verifiable reward settings. We hope future work will explore more robust RL algorithms that can handle the entropy increases required for creative reasoning. We also note that our infrastructure relies on Verl as the training backend and SGLang as the inference backend; their current joint support for structured, multi-step agentic frameworks is limited, and tighter integration would enable more scalable and reliable training pipelines.
blocks.zh: 鉴于我们任务固有的复杂性,特别是增加一个模型产出的内涵目标,我们发现,培训可能变得不稳定,特别是在更长的培训时间。 为低变异性,可核查的奖励设置而设计的标准RL算法所基于的稳定性假设与高率生成相悖. 我们希望今后的工作将探索更坚固的RL算法,能够处理创造性推理所需的 en增量. 我们还注意到,我们的基础设施依靠Verl作为培训后端,而SGLang作为推断后端;它们目前对结构化、多步骤代理框架的联合支持有限,更紧密的整合将使培训管道更加可扩展和可靠。
